questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country as I wanted to improve my legal English and have the biggest selection of elective s possible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, the school was good at sending out information in good time and the staff connected to the exchange students were fast at replying to emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The law program had an orientation week in the being of the semester. We were also matched with an exchange buddy we could reach out too.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Originally only Alumni House and Bayfiels House but I ended up at London Hall.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Both. I didn't have a meal plan - I also wouldn't recommend it. All housing options for exchange students had good cooking facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Overall nothing wrong with it everything was fine, but if you have/find other options I would recommended that. Normally it's only first years live in residence so you will end up living with 18-19 year olds. It is also cheeper to live off campus - however some areas are pretty sketchy.

If you want to live on campus I would recommend Alumni as you are more likely to live with other exchange student who are more likely to be closer in age to you.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's a point system. We were given 14 point (I think) to bit on the courses we wanted. Then there was an add and drop periode, where you could change the classes according to availability.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Western gave us a guide, and you could contact administration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: around 50/50

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: This more applies to KU but its easier to pick, add and drop courses so your schedule makes sense if you have merit from KU for as many courses as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was pretty much the same as KU, but expectations to attendance and participation was different - not bad just different. Attendance is mandatorily and the keep track - even if you don't think they do - and participation is typically a very small part of your grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The encouragement of participation and the lectures sometimes mostly felt like one long presentation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Environmental Law, International Business Transactions, Private Practise and Intellectual property rights

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Honestly, all of them. They were all pretty manageable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, you had to pay for your western one card, but it gave you free transport on busses. The busses didn't go after midnight so I did use a substantial amount of money on Ubers (and the bus system was also very bad in general).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food (except fresh produce) and eating out was very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot. everything from sport, food, outdoorsy things ect.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't personally do any, so idk. Those who did, did however seem to enjoy it a lot - an easy way to make friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside of London. London is very boring in itself, but you can catch a flixbus to toronto or rent a car and go to the Stats. For longer trips I recommend Montreal and Calgary - but you will ned more than a weekend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy after I got used to tipping.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are all very talkative and nice. Orientation give an opportunity otherwise there are other social events at Law (like dennings every two weeks).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They like to small talk A LOT. Even strangers on the street.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The small talk lol. You get use to it and the openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Explore Richmond street, use your exchange buddy and explore social events on campus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think, I've covered it

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met at school but also local.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to the teaching style, but honestly not to overwhelming.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
